# Method for Processing Ambient Audio Signals with Directional Transfer Functions

The disclosed method addresses the processing of multiple ambient audio signals through the application of directional transfer function pairs, enabling dynamic spatial audio rendering that responds to changes in target direction over time.

## Initial Signal Acquisition and Processing

The method begins by obtaining at least three ambient audio signals. Among these signals, at least one is processed using a first directional transfer function pair, while at least one other signal is processed using a second, distinct directional transfer function pair. The selection of which transfer function pair is applied to which signal is not arbitrary; rather, it is based on the respective target directions associated with each individual signal. This ensures that each ambient audio signal is spatially rendered in a manner consistent with its intended directional origin or destination within the audio scene.

## Assignment of Directional Transfer Function Pairs

The directional transfer function pairs assigned to each ambient audio signal are determined systematically according to the target directions linked to those signals. This means that the relationship between a given signal and its corresponding transfer function pair is governed by directional correspondence—signals associated with similar or identical target directions may share the same transfer function pair, while signals with differing target directions are processed using distinct pairs. This directional mapping establishes the foundational spatial characteristics of the ambient audio signals as they are initially processed.

## Detection of Target Direction Changes

A key feature of the method involves monitoring and determining when the target direction for at least one of the ambient audio signals changes to a new, updated target direction. This detection mechanism allows the method to remain responsive to dynamic changes in the desired spatial positioning of audio signals, which may occur due to changes in listener orientation, source movement, or other contextual factors within the audio environment. The method is thus capable of identifying, in real time or near-real time, when an existing directional assignment no longer accurately reflects the intended spatial placement of a given signal.

## Selection of an Updated Transfer Function Pair

Upon detecting a change in target direction, the method proceeds to select an updated directional transfer function pair from a plurality of available directional transfer functions. This selection process is guided by a comparative evaluation: the updated pair is chosen specifically because it demonstrates a closer association with the new, updated target direction than the originally assigned first directional transfer function pair. In other words, the method does not simply retain the original transfer function pair or apply an arbitrary substitute; instead, it actively searches among the available options to identify the pair that best matches the newly determined directional requirement.

## Continued and Updated Processing

Following the selection of the updated directional transfer function pair, the method applies this new pair to process the at least one ambient audio signal whose target direction has changed. Simultaneously, the method ensures continuity in the processing of the remaining ambient audio signals: the other ambient audio signal, whose target direction has not changed, continues to be processed using the original second directional transfer function pair. This selective updating mechanism allows the method to accommodate dynamic directional changes for specific signals without disrupting the processing of other signals that remain directionally stable, thereby maintaining overall coherence and accuracy in the spatial audio rendering process.

# Method and System for Adaptive Directional Audio Rendering

## Background and Overview

Spatial audio rendering systems are designed to reproduce the perception of sound arriving from specific directions relative to a listener, enabling immersive audio experiences in applications such as virtual reality, augmented reality, teleconferencing, and gaming. A core challenge in these systems is accurately representing multiple simultaneous sound sources whose apparent directions may change dynamically over time, while doing so efficiently enough to support real-time processing.

## Detailed Description of the Method

The disclosed method processes a plurality of ambient audio signals—at least three distinct signals—each of which is associated with a target direction indicating the spatial position from which that particular sound should appear to originate relative to the listener. To achieve accurate spatialization, each ambient audio signal is processed using a directional transfer function pair, which may include, for example, head-related transfer functions (HRTFs) or other binaural/ambisonic transfer function representations corresponding to left and right ear channels, or to specific loudspeaker feed configurations.

Rather than relying on a fixed, single transfer function pair for each signal, the system maintains a library or set comprising a plurality of directional transfer function pairs, each pre-associated with a discrete spatial direction or region. Upon initialization, each incoming ambient audio signal is assigned the transfer function pair from this set whose associated direction most closely matches the signal's specified target direction. This assignment process may involve calculating an angular distance or similarity metric between the target direction and each candidate transfer function pair's associated direction, then selecting the pair that minimizes this distance or maximizes this similarity.

## Dynamic Reassignment Mechanism

A key feature of the method is its capacity for dynamic adaptation. As the system operates, the target direction associated with any given ambient audio signal may change—for instance, due to movement of a virtual sound source, tracked motion of a physical sound-emitting object, or user interaction that repositions an audio element within the spatial scene. When such a change in target direction is detected for a particular signal, the system re-evaluates the available directional transfer function pairs and identifies whether a different pair, more closely aligned with the updated target direction, is available within the set.

If a more closely matching transfer function pair is identified, the system dynamically updates the assignment, substituting the previously used pair with the newly selected one for subsequent processing of that signal. This reassignment occurs on a per-signal basis: only the signal whose target direction has changed undergoes reassignment, while all other ambient audio signals—whose target directions remain unchanged—continue to be processed using their previously assigned transfer function pairs. This selective updating ensures computational efficiency, as unnecessary recalculations or reassignments are avoided for stationary or unchanged sound sources.

## Advantages and Technical Effects

This adaptive selection approach provides several technical benefits over static or continuously interpolated rendering methods. First, it enables real-time tracking of moving or repositioned sound sources with a granularity determined by the density of available transfer function pairs in the set, allowing the perceived direction of each ambient signal to be updated responsively as conditions change. Second, by isolating the reassignment process to only the affected signal, the method reduces computational overhead compared to approaches that would require recalculating transfer functions for all signals whenever any single target direction changes.

Furthermore, this approach improves the overall precision of the spatial audio rendering system, since each signal is consistently matched to the best-available directional transfer function pair based on current positional information, rather than relying on a coarse initial assignment that may become progressively inaccurate as the sound source moves. The combination of accurate initial assignment, continuous monitoring of target direction changes, and selective dynamic reassignment results in a spatial audio rendering system that is both computationally efficient and capable of delivering a high-fidelity, responsive listening experience—particularly valuable in interactive or dynamic audio environments where multiple sound sources may move independently and unpredictably relative to the listener.

## Implementation Considerations

The set of available directional transfer function pairs may be predetermined and stored in a lookup table, indexed by direction, to facilitate rapid searching and matching during both initial assignment and subsequent reassignment operations. The granularity of directional coverage provided by this set—that is, the angular spacing between the directions associated with successive transfer function pairs—may be selected based on the desired trade-off between spatial resolution and system resource constraints such as memory and processing capacity. In some implementations, the method may further incorporate smoothing or crossfading techniques when transitioning between transfer function pairs, in order to minimize any perceptible discontinuity in the rendered audio output at the moment of reassignment, thereby further enhancing the perceptual quality of the spatial audio rendering during dynamic tracking scenarios.

A method for processing multiple ambient audio signals, the method comprising:

receiving, via a plurality of microphones, a plurality of ambient audio signals from an acoustic environment;

determining a target direction relative to a reference orientation, wherein the target direction is subject to change over time based on at least one of a detected movement, a detected orientation change, or a received directional input;

selecting, from a stored set of directional transfer function pairs, a directional transfer function pair corresponding to the determined target direction, wherein each directional transfer function pair comprises a first transfer function associated with a first channel and a second transfer function associated with a second channel, and wherein each directional transfer function pair is associated with a distinct spatial direction relative to the reference orientation;

applying the selected directional transfer function pair to the plurality of ambient audio signals to generate a first processed audio signal and a second processed audio signal, wherein the first processed audio signal and the second processed audio signal collectively preserve directional audio cues corresponding to the target direction;

detecting a change in the target direction from a first target direction to a second target direction;

in response to detecting the change, selecting an updated directional transfer function pair corresponding to the second target direction from the stored set of directional transfer function pairs; and

applying the updated directional transfer function pair to the plurality of ambient audio signals to generate an updated first processed audio signal and an updated second processed audio signal, such that the directional audio cues are updated to correspond to the second target direction.

# PATENT ABSTRACT

## System and Method for Dynamic Directional Transfer Function Assignment in Ambient Audio Processing

### Abstract

A system and method for processing multiple ambient audio signals through directionally-differentiated transfer functions that dynamically update in response to changes in a target direction parameter. The system comprises an audio input module configured to receive a plurality of ambient audio signals from spatially distributed sources or microphone elements; a direction determination module configured to establish and continuously monitor a target direction relative to a reference point; a transfer function assignment module configured to associate each of the plurality of ambient audio signals with a distinct directional transfer function selected from a set of stored or computed transfer functions, wherein each transfer function encodes direction-dependent spectral, phase, and amplitude modification characteristics corresponding to a specific spatial relationship between the respective ambient audio signal's origin and the target direction; and an update module configured to detect changes in the target direction and, in response, recompute or reselect the directional transfer functions assigned to each ambient audio signal such that the directional relationship encoded by each transfer function remains consistent relative to the updated target direction. The system further comprises an audio output module configured to apply the updated transfer functions to the respective ambient audio signals and combine the processed signals into an output audio stream exhibiting perceptually accurate directional characteristics relative to the current target direction. The invention enables real-time spatial audio rendering that maintains directional coherence as a listener's orientation, a sound source's position, or a designated target changes, with applications in spatial audio rendering, hearing assistance devices, augmented and virtual reality systems, and directional audio capture and playback.

---

### Independent Claim 1

A system for dynamic directional audio processing, comprising:

**(a)** an input interface configured to receive a plurality of ambient audio signals, each ambient audio signal associated with a spatial origin relative to a reference frame;

**(b)** a memory storing a plurality of directional transfer functions, each directional transfer function defining a direction-dependent modification to at least one of amplitude, phase, or frequency spectrum of an audio signal;

**(c)** a processor operatively coupled to the input interface and the memory, configured to:
   (i) determine a current target direction relative to the reference frame;
   (ii) assign, to each of the plurality of ambient audio signals, a respective directional transfer function selected based on a spatial relationship between the spatial origin of said ambient audio signal and the current target direction, such that at least two of the ambient audio signals are assigned different directional transfer functions;
   (iii) apply the assigned directional transfer functions to the respective ambient audio signals to generate a plurality of processed audio signals;
   (iv) detect a change in the target direction from the current target direction to an updated target direction; and
   (v) in response to detecting the change, dynamically update the directional transfer function assigned to at least one of the ambient audio signals to reflect the spatial relationship between the spatial origin of said ambient audio signal and the updated target direction; and

**(d)** an output interface configured to combine the plurality of processed audio signals into a composite output audio signal.

### Dependent Claims (Illustrative)

**Claim 2:** The system of claim 1, wherein the processor updates the directional transfer functions substantially continuously in real time in response to a continuously varying target direction.

**Claim 3:** The system of claim 1, wherein the spatial origin of each ambient audio signal corresponds to a fixed microphone element position within a microphone array, and the target direction corresponds to a designated listening or focus direction.

**Claim 4:** The system of claim 1, wherein the directional transfer functions are head-related transfer functions (HRTFs) selected from a database indexed by relative azimuth and elevation angle.

**Claim 5:** The system of claim 1, wherein detecting the change in target direction comprises receiving sensor data indicative of a change in orientation of a wearable device.

**Claim 6:** The system of claim 1, wherein the processor is further configured to interpolate between a first directional transfer function and a second directional transfer function during a transition period following detection of the change in target direction, so as to produce a smoothed transition in the composite output audio signal.

**Claim 7:** The system of claim 1, wherein at least one directional transfer function is computed in real time as a function of the updated target direction, rather than selected from a predetermined set.

---

*Note: This document is a drafted template for illustrative purposes and does not constitute a filed or examined patent claim. Actual patent prosecution requires review by a licensed patent attorney or agent, prior art search, and jurisdiction-specific formatting (e.g., USPTO, EPO, PCT requirements).*

# Patent Application Draft

## TITLE OF THE INVENTION
**SYSTEM AND METHOD FOR SPATIAL AUDIO RENDERING USING MULTIPLE AMBIENT SIGNALS WITH DYNAMICALLY RESELECTABLE DIRECTIONAL TRANSFER FUNCTION PAIRS**

---

## FIELD OF THE INVENTION

The present invention relates generally to audio signal processing, and more particularly to systems and methods for rendering spatial audio using a plurality of ambient signal components, wherein each component is processed using a distinct pair of directional transfer functions selected from a set of candidate transfer function pairs, and wherein said selection is dynamically updated in response to changes in a target spatial direction associated with each ambient signal.

---

## BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION

Spatial audio rendering systems commonly employ head-related transfer functions (HRTFs) or other directional transfer functions to impart perceptual directionality to audio signals presented to a listener, typically via headphones or a loudspeaker array. Conventional approaches often apply a single transfer function pair to a monolithic audio signal, or interpolate between fixed transfer function measurements as a virtual sound source direction changes continuously.

Such conventional systems suffer from several deficiencies when applied to ambient, diffuse, or multi-component sound fields. First, continuous interpolation between transfer function measurements can introduce spectral artifacts, comb-filtering effects, or perceptually unstable localization cues, particularly when the underlying transfer function set is sparse. Second, treating an ambient sound field as a single directional entity fails to capture the perceptually important spatial diffuseness and multiplicity of apparent sound sources that characterize natural ambient environments. Third, existing systems generally do not provide independently reselectable transfer function pairs on a per-signal-component basis, limiting their ability to render complex, dynamically evolving spatial scenes with multiple concurrently active ambient sources.

There exists a need for a spatial audio rendering system that processes a plurality of ambient signal components independently, each with its own directional transfer function pair, and that can reselect said transfer function pairs discretely and independently as the associated directions evolve, while maintaining perceptual continuity and computational efficiency.

---

## SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

In accordance with one aspect of the present invention, there is provided a method for rendering spatial audio, comprising: receiving or generating at least three ambient signals, each ambient signal being associated with a respective target direction relative to a listener position; selecting, for each of the at least three ambient signals, a respective directional transfer function pair from a plurality of candidate directional transfer function pairs, each candidate pair being associated with a discrete spatial direction or region; processing each ambient signal by convolving or otherwise filtering said ambient signal with its respective selected directional transfer function pair to produce a plurality of directionally-rendered ambient signals; combining the plurality of directionally-rendered ambient signals to produce an output binaural or multi-channel audio signal; monitoring the respective target direction associated with each of the at least three ambient signals for a change; and, responsive to detecting a change in a given target direction that satisfies a reselection criterion, reselecting the directional transfer function pair for the corresponding ambient signal independently of the directional transfer function pairs selected for the other ambient signals.

In accordance with another aspect, the reselection may be performed using a crossfade, morph, or transition function between a previously selected transfer function pair and a newly selected transfer function pair, so as to mitigate audible discontinuities.

In accordance with a further aspect, the invention provides a corresponding apparatus comprising one or more processors, a memory storing a library of candidate directional transfer function pairs, and instructions executable to perform the method described above.

---

## BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF THE DRAWINGS

**FIG. 1** is a block diagram illustrating an exemplary spatial audio rendering system according to an embodiment of the invention.

**FIG. 2** is a flow diagram illustrating a method for processing a plurality of ambient signals using independently reselectable directional transfer function pairs.

**FIG. 3** illustrates an exemplary arrangement of candidate directional transfer function pairs distributed across a spatial region surrounding a listener.

**FIG. 4** is a signal flow diagram illustrating crossfading between a first and second directional transfer function pair responsive to a change in target direction.

**FIG. 5** illustrates an exemplary embodiment in which the ambient signals correspond to decorrelated components of a diffuse sound field.

---

## DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF THE PREFERRED EMBODIMENTS

### System Overview

Referring now to FIG. 1, there is shown an exemplary spatial audio rendering system 100 comprising a signal source module 110, an ambient signal generator 120, a direction determination module 130, a transfer function selection module 140, a transfer function library 150, a plurality of filtering/convolution engines 160a-160n, and a signal combiner 170, the output of which is provided to an audio output device 180 such as headphones or a loudspeaker array.

The ambient signal generator 120 is configured to generate or receive at least three ambient signals 122a, 122b, 122c (and optionally additional ambient signals 122n), each ambient signal representing a component of a spatial sound field. In one embodiment, the ambient signals are generated by decorrelating a common source signal using a plurality of decorrelation filters, such that the resulting ambient signals 122a-n are mutually incoherent or partially incoherent, thereby simulating a diffuse sound field when subsequently rendered with distinct directional cues. In an alternative embodiment, the ambient signals 122a-n are captured independently, for example from spatially distributed microphones, or are synthesized as independent noise or reverberant tail components.

### Direction Determination

The direction determination module 130 is configured to determine, for each ambient signal 122a-n, a respective target direction 132a-n relative to a reference listener position and orientation. The target directions 132a-n may be fixed, may be determined algorithmically (for example, to distribute ambient signals substantially uniformly about the listener), may be derived from metadata associated with an audio program, or may be dynamically updated in response to listener head tracking data, scene analysis, or user input.

It is a feature of the present invention that the target directions 132a-n associated with different ambient signals 122a-n are, in general, independent of one another, such that a change in the target direction of one ambient signal does not necessitate a corresponding change in the target direction of another ambient signal.

### Transfer Function Selection

The transfer function library 150 stores a plurality of candidate directional transfer function pairs 152, each candidate pair comprising, for example, a left-ear transfer function and a right-ear transfer function corresponding to a discrete spatial direction or angular region (e.g., azimuth and elevation combination) relative to the listener. In certain embodiments, the candidate directional transfer function pairs 152 comprise measured or modeled head-related transfer function (HRTF) pairs, though it will be appreciated that other directional transfer functions, such as binaural room impulse responses (BRIRs) or loudspeaker-array panning functions, may be substituted without departing from the scope of the invention.

The transfer function selection module 140 is configured to select, for each ambient signal 122a-n, a respective directional transfer function pair from the transfer function library 150 based on the corresponding target direction 132a-n. In a preferred embodiment, the selection comprises identifying, among the candidate directional transfer function pairs 152, the pair whose associated spatial direction is nearest, according to a defined distance metric (e.g., angular distance), to the target direction 132a-n. It will be appreciated that the selection need not involve continuous interpolation between candidate pairs, but may instead comprise a discrete, nearest-neighbor, or quantized selection, although interpolated or blended selection is contemplated as an alternative embodiment.

Notably, because each ambient signal 122a-n has an independently determined target direction 132a-n, the transfer function selection module 140 may select a distinct directional transfer function pair for each ambient signal, such that at a given time, the first ambient signal 122a is processed with a first directional transfer function pair, the second ambient signal 122b is processed with a second, different directional transfer function pair, and the third ambient signal 122c is processed with a third, different directional transfer function pair.

### Filtering and Combination

Each of the filtering/convolution engines 160a-n is configured to filter its respective ambient signal 122a-n using the currently selected directional transfer function pair, for example by convolving the ambient signal with the left-ear and right-ear impulse responses of the selected pair, to produce a directionally-rendered left-channel component and a directionally-rendered right-channel component for that ambient signal.

The signal combiner 170 is configured to sum, or otherwise combine, the directionally-rendered left-channel components from each of the filtering/convolution engines 160a-n to produce a composite left-channel output signal, and to similarly combine the directionally-rendered right-channel components to produce a composite right-channel output signal, the composite left-channel and right-channel output signals together forming a binaural output signal for presentation via the audio output device 180.

### Dynamic Reselection

Referring now to FIG. 2, there is illustrated a method 200 for dynamically reselecting directional transfer function pairs. At step 210, the system monitors the target direction associated with each ambient signal. At step 220, for a given ambient signal, the system determines whether the associated target direction has changed by an amount exceeding a reselection threshold, or whether the target direction now falls within the angular region associated with a different candidate transfer function pair. If so, at step 230, the system selects a new directional transfer function pair for that ambient signal from the transfer function library, independently of the transfer function pairs currently selected for the other ambient signals. At step 240, the system transitions the filtering operation for that ambient signal from the previous directional transfer function pair to the newly selected directional transfer function pair.

In a preferred embodiment, the transition of step 240 is performed using a crossfade technique, wherein the ambient signal is concurrently filtered using both the previous and newly selected directional transfer function pairs over a transition interval, and the respective outputs are combined using a time-varying weighting function (e.g., a linear, equal-power, or raised-cosine crossfade) such that the contribution of the previous transfer function pair diminishes to zero and the contribution of the newly selected transfer function pair increases to unity over the transition interval. This crossfading approach mitigates audible artifacts, such as clicks or discontinuities, that might otherwise arise from an abrupt switch between transfer function pairs.

In an alternative embodiment, the transition is achieved by interpolating the impulse responses or frequency-domain representations of the previous and newly selected transfer function pairs, rather than by crossfading their respective filtered outputs.

It is a feature of certain embodiments that the reselection determination and transition process described above is performed independently and asynchronously for each of the plurality of ambient signals, such that at any given time, some ambient signals may be undergoing a transition between transfer function pairs while others remain statically filtered with a previously selected pair.

### Exemplary Embodiment: Diffuse Field Rendering

Referring to FIG. 5, in one exemplary embodiment, the ambient signal generator 120 receives a single source ambient signal (e.g., a reverberant tail or diffuse noise-like signal) and generates the at least three ambient signals 122a-n by applying a plurality of substantially decorrelating filters (e.g., all-pass filters with distinct phase responses) to the source ambient signal. The resulting decorrelated ambient signals 122a-n are then assigned target directions 132a-n that are distributed about the listener, for example at azimuthal positions substantially equally spaced about a horizontal plane, or according to a pseudo-random distribution updated periodically to simulate an evolving diffuse field. This arrangement advantageously produces a perceptually diffuse, enveloping spatial impression while permitting the individual directional cues
